instruction: The last sweater I bought on Amazon is a bit too large for me. Initiate a return for it, and buy a replacement of the same in the next smaller size. If it's available now in red, prefer it, otherwise go with the same color.
notes: Fix: the predicate previously named last-sweater collided with the object last-sweater; the predicate is now is-last-sweater (all other names are unique across types, predicates, constants and objects). Single-app (amazon) task plus supervisor. The last sweater purchase and its order are pre-existing entities whose ids are discovered by show_product_purchases; show_product on that sweater reveals its size/color variations, making the replacement variant (next smaller size, red if available else same color -- selection rule lives in the binding) known. The return needs a deliverer id from show_return_deliverers; the replacement is added to the cart with quantity 1 and clear_cart_first=true so the new order contains exactly one item of quantity 1, then the order is placed with a looked-up payment card and existing address (addresses are never modified). supervisor.complete_task takes the task records as non-API parameters so its precondition equals the goal; it is forced to be last via (not (task-completed)) on every other action.
